record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: Beyond Pareto-optimal and stable matchings, study the complexity and algorithmics of fairness notions such as popular matchings and rank-maximal matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain under the lottery, compact-indifference, or related uncertainty models.

evidence.quote: After Pareto optimal and stable matchings, one might consider to investigate other fairness notions under uncertain preferences, such as popular or rank-maximal matchings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bipartite matching market with a set of agents on each side (or a one-sided market with agents and indivisible items). Each agent has preferences over the agents/items on the opposite side, but these preferences are uncertain and are described by one of the following uncertainty models:

1. Lottery model: for each agent, an independent probability distribution over strict linear orders of the other side is given.
2. Compact-indifference model: for each agent, a weak order (with ties) is given, and each strict linear order consistent with this weak order is assumed equally likely.
3. Joint probability model: a probability distribution is given over complete preference profiles.

Given a matching M between the two sides, recall:
- M is popular if there is no other matching M' such that the number of agents preferring M' to M exceeds the number preferring M to M'.
- M is rank-maximal (in the one-sided setting with ranked preferences) if it lexicographically maximizes the vector (x_1, x_2, ..., x_n), where x_i is the number of agents matched to a partner ranked i-th.

Problem. For each of the uncertainty models above and for each of the natural decision variants (e.g., does there exist a matching that is popular/rank-maximal with probability 1; does there exist a matching whose probability of being popular/rank-maximal exceeds a given threshold; compute a matching maximizing such a probability), determine the computational complexity. Provide either polynomial-time algorithms or hardness results (e.g., NP-hardness, #P-hardness) in both the one-sided (house allocation type) setting and the two-sided (marriage type) setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (Boehmer, Heeger, et al., "Popular and Dominant Matchings with Uncertain, Multilayer and Aggregated Preferences", arXiv:2310.14288) addresses popular matchings under the lottery, compact-indifference, joint-probability, and multilayer models. In the one-sided setting most variants are shown to be polynomial-time solvable, while in the two-sided setting all four models lead to NP-hard problems (e.g., deciding the existence of a certainly popular matching is NP-hard, even when one side has fixed preferences). Rank-maximal matchings under these uncertainty models appear less thoroughly studied, so the overall research direction is partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Popular and Dominant Matchings with Uncertain, Multilayer and Aggregated Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: First comprehensive study of popular matchings under uncertain and multilayered preferences; one-sided variants are polynomial-time solvable while two-sided variants under lottery, compact-indifference, and joint-probability models are NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: Popular matchings under the listed uncertainty models have been substantially analyzed, with both polynomial-time algorithms (one-sided) and NP-hardness results (two-sided).

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces lottery, compact-indifference, and joint-probability models for stable matching and analyzes their complexity.
status_evidence.claim: The uncertainty models referenced (lottery, compact-indifference) are formalized and used in related work on stable matching.
